name: Jack Monroe
summary: A former detective with a frayed conscience, a stubborn instinct for the truth, and a history with the Ray family.
look: Salt-and-pepper dark hair, worn brown tweed jacket, open charcoal shirt, dark trousers and scuffed shoes.
continuity: Carries sunflower seeds, never a lollipop. After Tick shoots his thigh, the wound persists and Jack does not walk again in the film.

name: Vera Voss
summary: Corn's sharp-eyed bookkeeper knows where the numbers are buried, and what she has done to protect herself.
look: Dark bob, fitted chocolate-brown suit, cream blouse, leather heels and a ledger kept close.
continuity: Her handwriting gives away the tip to Harriett. She admits the rigged clock and leaves her own pages in the ledger.

name: Etta Ray
summary: Bug and Peanut's mother; dignified, warm and fiercely unwilling to let her son's death be dismissed.
look: Short natural hair touched with gray, gold hoops, burgundy wrap dress, dark cardigan and practical heels.
continuity: Etta keeps the ledger and copies, and publicly names Tick, Pike and Kellerman. Her composure never erases her grief.

name: Bug Ray
summary: Etta's observant younger son, always listening for a rhythm and carrying his shoebox recorder.
look: Short natural hair, denim jacket and jeans, plain T-shirt, canvas sneakers and a portable cassette recorder.
continuity: A kid, not an adult. His final dryer rhythm is made with physical tape splicing and a dubbed loop, not a sampler; Peanut's laugh comes first.

name: Peanut Ray
summary: Etta's older son is funny, kind and handsome; his laugh and a small piece of paperwork outlive him.
look: Short rounded Afro, brown leather jacket, earth-toned collared knit, dark jeans and worn shoes.
continuity: He folds laundry in the cold open. Bug's tape preserves his laugh and the voice of the man with the gold pinky ring.

name: Harriett
summary: A Panther organizer who feeds neighborhood children and weighs the cost before she sends people into danger.
look: Full natural Afro, dark leather coat, burgundy turtleneck, high-waisted dark trousers and sturdy boots.
continuity: Vera sends her into a rigged clock. Harriett counts her people, confronts Vera, and takes the sealed dope to the Hudson.

name: Dove
summary: Harriett's protective, skeptical colleague, just as comfortable making sandwiches as questioning a dangerous tip.
look: Rounded natural Afro, brown suede jacket, rust knit shirt, dark jeans and black boots.
continuity: He is shot in the shoulder during the warehouse fight and wears a sling afterward.

name: Cornelius “Corn” Brandt
summary: Sal's careful fixer hires Jack, keeps the dangerous ledger close and trusts figures more than people.
look: Slicked-back silver hair, dark checked three-piece suit, patterned tie, polished shoes and a slim ledger.
continuity: Jack gives Corn's payment to Etta. Corn dies looking for the shoe he lost, without a poetic last line.

name: Lt. Frank Pike
summary: A patient, corrupt officer who uses his authority to keep the paper trail and its witnesses under control.
look: Close-cut gray hair, open dark overcoat, rumpled detective's suit and a loosened wide tie.
continuity: He shoots Tick to silence him, panics in the gunfight, then faces an investigation and gives up his badge.

name: Tick Lane
summary: A guarded dealer whose visible gold pinky ring connects him to the voice on Peanut's recording.
look: Dark wavy hair, long dark coat, black shirt, leather gloves and a distinctive gold pinky ring.
continuity: He shoots Jack, is gut-shot by Pike and dies slowly reaching for the recorder. Keep the ring consistent with the opening glimpse.

name: Nicky
summary: A precise, conscientious clerk who keeps his records straight even when the room is coming apart.
look: Soft dark hair, brown cardigan, collared shirt and tie, pencil, clipboard and neatly pressed trousers.
continuity: He is procedural, not a stutterer. He keeps logging the gunfight until a stray round kills him.

name: Whitney Kellerman
summary: The city property official whose impressive seal makes a criminal transfer look like ordinary paperwork.
look: Neat graying hair, dark three-piece suit, patterned tie, ink-marked cuff and oversized wood-handled stamp.
continuity: He hides under the table, cuts his hand and later faces questioning; the stamp becomes evidence.

name: Clutch
summary: A big man with a soft face who came to the auction for a pinball machine and got caught between everyone else.
look: Broad build, dark beard, weathered leather vest, work shirt, dark jeans, boots and a plain cap.
continuity: The Spirit of '76 flyer and pinball machine identify him. He is the innocent bystander killed in the warehouse.

name: Sal Vetrano
summary: Corn's employer, a watchful presence at the coffee shop whose people are waiting at the warehouse.
look: Salt-and-pepper hair, dark blazer, cream waistcoat, open-collared shirt and an espresso cup.
continuity: Sal's crew is part of the warehouse deal; Corn handles his books and is the one who hires Jack.
